historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Historical CAGRs materially overstate the current trajectory. The 5yr revenue CAGR (20.3%) captures 2020-2022 hypergrowth/COVID reopening and is not usable. The 3yr revenue CAGR (11.0%) still reflects the FY2023 inventory-normalization snapback. The most decision-relevant historical anchor is the FY2023-FY2025 2yr CAGR of 7.4%/yr, and even that overstates the near term: FY2026 company guidance (cut June 4, 2026) calls for roughly flat revenue ($11.0-11.15B vs FY2025's $11.10B) and EPS of $10.95-11.15 (down from $13.26, a mid-teens % decline) as tariffs compress margins ~400-700bp. FCF CAGRs are not usable as anchors: the 3yr FCF CAGR (41.1%) is inflated by a depressed FY2022 base (capex surge/inventory build, $327.8M), and the 5yr (9.9%) understates the current run rate because FY2025's $921.7M FCF is itself a tariff-depressed trough. Equity CAGR (14.2%/16.4%) is structurally understated by ~$1.0-1.2B/yr buybacks reducing book value mechanically, so it is not a reliable base-case anchor either. Given this, the model does not select a single trailing CAGR as the forward growth rate; it anchors Year 1 explicitly to FY2026 guidance (flat-to-declining FCF) and builds a decelerating-to-modest recovery path in Years 2-5, well below all trailing multi-year revenue/EPS CAGRs.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Significant divergence across all growth metrics (FCF 3yr 41.1% vs 5yr 9.9%; revenue 3yr 11.0% vs 5yr 20.3%) is event-driven, not structural: FY2022 was an FCF/inventory trough, FY2020-2021 was COVID-reopening hypergrowth, and FY2025 is a fresh tariff-driven trough ($275M gross tariff impact). None of the trailing CAGRs is used directly; the model instead anchors to FY2026 management guidance (flat revenue, EPS down ~15-17%) as the near-term reality and builds the recovery path from qualitative catalysts (supply-chain diversification, new CEO Heidi O'Neill starting Sept 2026, China growth) rather than extrapolating any single historical CAGR.

historical_fcf_series.note: FY2022 depressed by capex surge and inventory build. FY2023/24 benefited from inventory normalization (do not use as base). FY2025 depressed by $275M gross tariff hit and is the model's starting base.

base.name: Base Case: Guided Trough, Gradual Multi-Year Recovery
base.description: FY2026 (Y1) FCF declines further from the FY2025 base of $921.7M as tariffs escalate (Vietnam ~20% rate announced late July 2026, ~40% of sourcing), gross margin stays compressed (Q1 FY2026 already -410bp YoY), and Americas comps remain negative (-5% in Q1). This is consistent with FY2026 guidance of roughly flat revenue and EPS down to $10.95-11.15 from $13.26. From FY2027 (Y2) once new CEO Heidi O'Neill (started Sept 2026) resets execution, supply-chain diversification (Bangladesh/Indonesia/India) progressively reduces tariff drag, 'modest' pricing actions offset some cost pressure, and China Mainland/Rest of World continue at a decelerating-but-still-double-digit pace. Growth normalizes to mid-single-digit revenue/FCF growth by Y4-Y5 as the business settles into a structurally lower-margin, no-longer-hypergrowth steady state. FCF recovers to roughly $1.15B by FY2030 — still below the FY2023/24 peak ($1.6B) reflecting a permanently higher tariff/cost baseline.
base.growth_rate_reasoning: Y1 (-8%): FY2026 guided EPS decline (~-15 to -17%) is worse than FCF decline because buybacks and modest capex discipline partially cushion FCF; FCF falls from $921.7M to ~$848M. Y2 (+8%): New CEO in seat for a full year, tariff mitigation (pricing + sourcing shift) begins, Americas stabilizes off a very weak base, China still double-digit. Y3 (+10%): Supply-chain diversification gains traction, operating leverage returns as revenue growth resumes modestly. Y4 (+8%) / Y5 (+6%): Growth decelerates toward a sustainable mature-brand rate as China itself decelerates and Americas normalizes to low-single-digit growth; terminal growth (2.5%) approached but not yet reached by Y5.
base.wacc_reasoning: CAPM: risk-free rate ~4.3% + equity risk premium ~5.0% x beta ~1.15 = ~10.0%. Beta modestly above 1.0 reflects consumer discretionary cyclicality, an unresolved leadership transition (CEO started Sept 2026 but track record unproven at LULU), and tariff/trade-policy uncertainty. Zero debt means WACC = cost of equity with no leverage adjustment.

bull.name: Bull Case: Turnaround Under New CEO Succeeds
bull.description: Heidi O'Neill's Nike-honed brand/product playbook takes hold quickly: the product reset (post the January 2026 sheerness controversy and underwhelming launches) regains full-price sell-through, Americas comps turn positive by mid-FY2027, and brand-trust incidents (PFAS probe, proxy-fight optics) fade as one-time noise rather than lasting damage. Trade tensions ease enough that the ~20% Vietnam tariff rate is negotiated down or offset faster than expected via sourcing diversification. China Mainland decelerates only modestly (stays in the high-teens/20%+ range) as store expansion into new geographies (India, Rest of World) adds a second growth leg. FCF recovers strongly to approach the FY2023/24 pre-tariff peak (~$1.6-1.7B) by FY2030, but the model still does NOT assume a return to the 28x+ FY2024 P/E — only a partial re-rating toward the upper end of the modern (non-hypergrowth) range.
bull.growth_rate_reasoning: Y1 (+2%): Cost actions and pricing modestly outrun the tariff hit even in FY2026, holding FCF roughly flat/up slightly vs FY2025. Y2 (+20%): CEO transition executes cleanly; Americas inflects positive; tariff relief begins meaningfully. Y3 (+18%): Full supply-chain diversification benefit; China still compounding; operating leverage returns strongly. Y4 (+14%) / Y5 (+10%): Growth decelerates as the business matures at a larger, more international revenue base, but still well above the base case's terminal trajectory.
bull.wacc_reasoning: Lower WACC of 9% reflects resolved governance/leadership uncertainty (successful CEO transition), reduced tariff-policy risk, and a demonstrated return to growth reducing the equity risk premium demanded.

bear.name: Bear Case: Structural Americas Decline + China Offset Fails
bear.description: Americas comp declines (-5% in Q1 FY2026 and worsening per July 2026 channel checks from Jefferies/JPMorgan/Truist) prove structural: Alo Yoga and Vuori have permanently captured share, brand-trust damage from the sheerness/PFAS controversies does not fully heal, and the CEO transition (O'Neill, an outsider whose Nike tenure itself struggled recently) fails to arrest the decline through FY2027. Tariffs remain elevated (Vietnam ~20%, ~40% of sourcing) with slow diversification. China Mainland decelerates sharply toward 10% or below as Maia Active and other domestic brands underprice LULU by roughly half, especially in the lower-tier cities where LULU is now expanding. FCF stays trapped in the $700-820M range through the projection window with no structural catalyst, consistent with the guidance's own admission of a mid-teens EPS decline turning into a multi-year earnings recession rather than a one-year dip.
bear.growth_rate_reasoning: Y1 (-20%): FY2026 is worse than guided as tariffs bite harder than the $10.95-11.15 EPS guide implies and Americas comps deteriorate further into H2; FCF falls to ~$737M, consistent with the bear-case $700-800M sustained range. Y2 (0%): No recovery; CEO transition disappoints or is too slow; Americas still negative. Y3-Y5 (+3-4%): Marginal stabilization as China's remaining growth (even at a decelerated 10-12%) and modest cost discipline provide a small offset, but Americas never meaningfully recovers and FCF stays in the mid-$700M-$820M range throughout.
bear.wacc_reasoning: Higher WACC of 11.5% reflects elevated execution risk (unproven new CEO, structural competitive share loss, unresolved tariff/trade uncertainty extending past FY2029) and a business with a declining/impaired growth profile requiring a higher required return. Zero debt remains a partial offset limiting the WACC premium versus a levered peer in similar distress.

base.interpretation: At $113.37, the market is priced only ~3.4% above the base-case 15%-IRR entry price of $109.52. This is a materially different signal than a hypergrowth-anchored model would show: because base-case FCF growth (~-8%/+8%/+10%/+8%/+6%) is itself modest, the 15% hurdle sits well above the underlying growth path, so the entry price lands close to (not far below) intrinsic value. In plain terms: at today's price, achieving a 15% annualized return in the base case is plausible, not a distant reach — LULU is trading close to a fair, disciplined entry point in the base case.

bull.interpretation: In the bull case, the 15%-IRR entry price is $173.36 — 53% above the current price of $113.37. If the turnaround under the new CEO succeeds as modeled, today's price offers a substantial margin of safety relative to a 15% target return.

bear.interpretation: In the bear case, the 15%-IRR entry price is $73.29, about 35% below the current price. If Americas decline proves structural and China fails to offset it, an investor buying today would fall well short of a 15% annualized return and should expect capital loss.

sensitivity.matrix_note: All cells use base-case FCF growth path [-8%, +8%, +10%, +8%, +6%] starting from FY2025 base FCF of $921.7M. Rows = WACC (8-12%), Columns = Terminal Growth Rate (1.5-3.5%). Values are intrinsic value per share in USD. Current price of $113.37 plots almost exactly at WACC 10% / terminal growth 2.5% ($130.37, the base case itself) to WACC 11% / terminal growth 2.0-2.5% (~$111-116) -- i.e. the market is pricing something close to, or slightly more conservative than, our base case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Base case (50%) reflects the most probable path: FY2026 guidance is already a trough (EPS down mid-teens %, roughly flat revenue), followed by a gradual multi-year recovery as the new CEO (Heidi O'Neill, started Sept 2026), supply-chain diversification, and continued (decelerating) China growth combine to lift FCF back toward $1.1-1.2B by FY2030 -- still below the FY2023/24 peak. Bull (25%) reflects a real, but not base-case, possibility that the turnaround executes faster and more completely than guided, given O'Neill's Nike scaling pedigree and the resolved governance overhang (Chip Wilson proxy settlement, May 2026). Bear (25%) reflects genuine, currently-materializing structural risk: Americas comps have now declined for multiple consecutive quarters and are worsening (not improving) as of Q1 FY2026, management itself has attributed weakness partly to brand-sentiment damage (a harder problem than a normal product cycle), China deceleration is running ahead of guidance in some channel checks, and two consecutive guidance cuts within 90 days have damaged forecast credibility. The bear weight is not higher than 25% because: (1) zero debt and $1.5B net cash provide a real equity floor; (2) DTC gross margins in the mid-50s% remain well above typical apparel peers even after compression; (3) China and Rest of World are still growing (just more slowly), providing a genuine (if weakening) offset.

valuation_philosophy.approach: This DCF anchors to FY2025 FCF of $921.7M -- itself a tariff-depressed trough relative to the FY2023/24 range of $1.58-1.64B -- and explicitly does not assume a snap-back to those peak levels. The base case treats FY2026 as a further trough year (consistent with the company's own guidance of a mid-teens EPS decline) before a gradual, multi-year recovery driven by supply-chain diversification away from ~40% Vietnam sourcing, 'modest' pricing actions, and a new CEO mandate, arriving at roughly $1.15B FCF by FY2030 -- meaningfully below the FY2023/24 peak, reflecting a structurally higher tariff/cost baseline rather than a full return to the old margin structure. The bear case treats the current $700-900M FCF range as a durable new floor if Americas decline is structural and China deceleration continues. Because LULU carries zero long-term debt and $1.51B in cash, the equity floor is well supported even in the bear case.
valuation_philosophy.fcf_vs_earnings_note: FCF remains the more reliable anchor than EPS for LULU: FY2025 net income of $1,579.2M vs FCF of $921.7M reflects $680.8M of capex (store growth, supply-chain investment) that is real cash outflow, and FY2026 capex is guided at a similarly elevated $725-745M. EPS is also more exposed than FCF to the buyback-driven share count decline (115.4M diluted shares as of Q1 FY2026, down from 127.1M in FY2023, a ~4%/yr shrink), which can flatter EPS trends relative to the underlying cash-generative reality.
valuation_philosophy.buyback_effect: LULU intends to repurchase ~$1.2B in FY2026 (similar to FY2025), though only ~$1.0B remained under the $4.0B authorization as of May 3, 2026 after $361.8M of Q1 buybacks plus a further $111.0M through late May. At the current price (~$113), $1.1-1.2B retires roughly 10M shares (~8-9% of the 115.4M base), providing a meaningful structural EPS/per-share-value tailwind even in a flat-FCF environment. However, a materially lower earnings base means the same dollar buyback budget now buys back a larger share-count percentage than in prior years -- this is captured qualitatively rather than mechanically compounded into the per-share DCF, since the model already values total equity and divides by a static current share count.
valuation_philosophy.sensitivity_interpretation: The sensitivity matrix shows the current price of $113.37 sits almost exactly on the base case itself (WACC 10%/TG 2.5% = $130.37 is the single largest cell nearest the actual market price, with WACC~10.7%/TG~2.3% implied). This is a materially different read than a distressed-multiple story: the market is not pricing LULU as a broken business requiring heroic recovery assumptions to justify today's price -- it is pricing something close to our disciplined base case. Upside to base case IV (+15%) is real but modest; the larger opportunity is asymmetric on the bull case (+92%) if the CEO transition executes, while the bear case (-28%) is a plausible but not catastrophic downside given the net-cash balance sheet.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip: base-case IV $130.37 implies 10.6x TTM P/E / 11.8x forward P/E, below even the FY2025 trough multiple (13.2x) and far below the FY2024 modern-range 28.3x. Stock is in the lower half of its 10yr range; no re-rating assumed in base case.

historical_ranges.pe_hypergrowth_range_exclude: 37-73x (FY2018-FY2022, COVID/hypergrowth era -- excluded as DCF anchor)
historical_ranges.pb_modern_range: 4.2-11.9x (FY2024/FY2025, understated by aggressive buybacks reducing book value)
historical_ranges.note: FY2018-FY2022 multiples (37-73x P/E) reflect a hypergrowth/COVID-reopening era that will not recur and are explicitly excluded as sanity anchors per instruction. FY2024 (28.3x) and FY2025 (13.2x) bracket the relevant 'modern' comparison range for a maturing, tariff-challenged premium retailer.

exit_multiple_cap_check.verdict: No cap triggered. Base case implied exit EV/FCF multiple of 13.7x is essentially in line with today's actual EV/FCF of 12.55x -- the model assumes almost no multiple expansion, just modest FCF recovery. Bull case's 17.2x implies a partial re-rating (well below the FY2024 P/E-equivalent premium range and far below the hypergrowth-era 25-50x+ EV/EBIT multiples) consistent with a successful but not euphoric turnaround. Bear case's 10.7x implies mild further de-rating consistent with continued fundamental deterioration, not a re-rating assumption at all.

sanity_check.verdict: PASS. Base case IV of $130.37 implies a TTM P/E of 10.6x and forward (FY26 guide) P/E of 11.8x -- both BELOW the FY2025 trough multiple of 13.2x and far below the FY2024 modern-range multiple of 28.3x. This means the base case is not assuming any re-rating at all; it is assuming the stock stays at a depressed multiple while FCF modestly recovers, and even so land at a 15% upside. The bull case (17.6-19.7x P/E, 5.2x P/B) implies a partial re-rating toward the low end of the FY2024 modern range -- plausible if the CEO transition succeeds, but explicitly does NOT reach the FY2024 28.3x level, let alone the hypergrowth-era 40-73x range. The bear case (6.6-7.4x P/E) implies further multiple compression below even today's 9.2x TTM level, consistent with a scenario where fundamentals keep deteriorating. Given the stock trades in the lower half of its 10-year range and multiples have already collapsed to multi-year lows, the base case's modest (+15%) upside without any multiple expansion is a conservative, credible result -- not an artifact of unrealistic re-rating assumptions.

key_assumptions_summary.wacc_chosen: 10% base, 9% bull, 11.5% bear. CAPM-derived (rf ~4.3% + ERP ~5.0% x beta ~1.15 = ~10.0%) for base. Beta modestly above 1.0 reflects consumer discretionary cyclicality plus unresolved leadership-transition and tariff-policy risk. No leverage adjustment (zero debt).
key_assumptions_summary.terminal_growth_chosen: 2.5% base, 3.0% bull, 2.0% bear. Below nominal GDP growth (~4%), appropriate for a maturing premium apparel brand facing structural Americas competition, with China/international providing a modest above-GDP offset in the base/bull cases.
key_assumptions_summary.base_fcf_note: FY2025 FCF of $921.7M is used as the starting base despite being itself tariff-depressed ($275M gross tariff impact). Year 1 (FY2026) projects a further decline to ~$848M, consistent with FY2026 guidance of a mid-teens EPS decline (to $10.95-11.15 from $13.26) as tariffs escalate (Vietnam ~20% rate announced late July 2026) and Americas comps remain negative.
key_assumptions_summary.recovery_path_logic: Supply-chain diversification away from ~40% Vietnam sourcing (toward Bangladesh/Indonesia/India) is a multi-year process; the model assumes meaningful tariff-drag reduction beginning Y2-Y3 (FY2027-2028) as the new CEO (Heidi O'Neill, started Sept 2026) resets execution. China Mainland/Rest of World continue to grow (decelerating from FY2025's 29% toward the low-to-mid teens by the out years) providing a structural offset to Americas maturity, but the model does not assume the China growth rate holds at Q1 FY2026's +20% -- further deceleration is embedded.
key_assumptions_summary.net_cash_significance: The $1.51B net cash position (zero debt) adds approximately $13.13/share in direct equity value support above the pure DCF-of-operations value. This meaningfully underpins the bear case ($81.65, -28% from current) as a plausible-but-not-catastrophic outcome rather than a solvency-risk scenario.

valuation_context.ev_ebit_note: EV/EBIT (FY2025 operating income $2,210.6M) at the current price is ~5.2x -- far below the FY2024/FY2025 modern range (8.6-19.7x) and the hypergrowth-era range (20-51x). This reflects the market pricing in prolonged earnings/margin pressure from tariffs and Americas weakness, consistent with the stock trading near its 52-week low.
valuation_context.buyback_context: LULU has guided to ~$1.2B in FY2026 share repurchases, similar to FY2025's pace, though only ~$1.0B remained under the $4.0B cumulative authorization as of May 3, 2026. At ~$113/share, this retires approximately 10.6M shares (~9% of the 115.4M diluted share base). Share count could fall toward ~108-110M by end of FY2026, providing a per-share value/EPS tailwind that partially offsets the earnings decline from tariffs and softer Americas demand -- though a lower earnings base means the same dollar buyback budget buys back a larger percentage of a smaller company than in prior high-growth years.
